title: Introduction to Industrial Engineering
description: This syllabus is designed as an entry point into industrial and systems engineering: students learn how IE improves work systems through measurement, modeling, people-centered design, quality, operations, analytics, and continuous improvement.

topics.title: Industrial Engineering Profession, Roles, and Career Pathways
topics.description: Introduce industrial and systems engineering as a profession focused on improving complex work systems.

children.title: What Industrial Engineers Improve
children.description: Students learn the scope of IE: not one machine or one department, but whole systems of work.

children.title: Industrial engineering, systems engineering, operations engineering, and process improvement
People, machines, materials, information, money, energy, and time as system elements
Manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, retail, aviation, public services, finance, and technology systems
Productivity, quality, safety, cost, delivery, sustainability, and customer experience
Career Roles and Professional Identity
children.description: This subtopic helps students see how the major leads into real jobs and professional communities.

children.title: Industrial engineer, operations analyst, quality engineer, process improvement analyst, manufacturing engineer, and supply chain analyst
Operations research analyst, ergonomist, simulation analyst, facilities planner, and continuous improvement specialist
IISE, INFORMS, ASQ, ASCM, HFES, and professional certifications
Consulting, internal improvement teams, engineering management, and analytics pathways
Historical Development and Modern IE
children.description: The point is to connect classic IE tools to modern analytics and human-centered systems.

children.title: Scientific management, time study, motion study, Gilbreth, Taylor, Gantt, Shewhart, Deming, and Toyota Production System
Operations research, systems thinking, human factors, quality engineering, and supply chain management
Digital transformation, Industry 4.0, automation, data analytics, AI, and cyber-physical systems
Ethics, worker dignity, safety, equity, and sustainable productivity

topics.title: Systems Thinking and Process View of Organizations
topics.description: Develop the habit of seeing organizations as connected systems of people, materials, information, equipment, and decisions.

children.title: Systems Concepts
children.description: Students learn vocabulary for describing interconnected work systems.

children.title: System boundary, environment, input, output, feedback, constraint, and stakeholder
Subsystem, interface, dependency, delay, feedback loop, and emergent behavior
Open system, closed system, socio-technical system, and complex adaptive system
Local optimum, global optimum, trade-off, and unintended consequence
Process Mapping and Flow
children.description: The goal is to make work visible before trying to improve it.

children.title: Process map, flowchart, SIPOC, swimlane diagram, value stream map, and spaghetti diagram
Activity, queue, delay, transport, inspection, rework, and handoff
Cycle time, lead time, throughput, work-in-process, and bottleneck
Voice of customer, voice of process, and process owner
System Performance and Feedback
children.description: This subtopic connects process structure to measured outcomes.

children.title: Feedback control, reinforcing loop, balancing loop, stock, flow, and delay
Capacity, demand, variability, utilization, and service level
Causal loop diagram and simple stock-flow thinking
Operations examples: emergency department, warehouse, production line, call center, and airport security

topics.title: Productivity, Efficiency, Effectiveness, and Performance Measurement
topics.description: Define how industrial engineers measure performance, value, waste, productivity, and system outcomes.

children.title: Productivity and Efficiency Measures
children.description: Students learn how IE quantifies output relative to resources.

children.title: Labor productivity, machine productivity, multifactor productivity, and total factor productivity
Efficiency, effectiveness, utilization, yield, throughput, and capacity
Standard time, actual time, earned hours, and labor variance
Value-added time, non-value-added time, and process cycle efficiency
Performance Metrics and Dashboards
children.description: The point is to choose metrics that reflect the system's real goals.

children.title: Key performance indicator, balanced scorecard, leading indicator, and lagging indicator
Cost, quality, delivery, safety, morale, sustainability, and flexibility metrics
On-time delivery, defect rate, first-pass yield, takt attainment, and customer wait time
Metric definition, data source, owner, frequency, and target
Trade-Offs and Measurement Pitfalls
children.description: Students learn that bad metrics can distort behavior.

children.title: Goodhart's law, gaming, suboptimization, vanity metric, and metric overload
Short-term versus long-term performance
Efficiency versus resilience, utilization versus waiting time, and cost versus quality
Data validity, operational definition, denominator choice, and fairness

topics.title: Problem-Solving Methodology and Engineering Improvement Projects
topics.description: Introduce structured problem solving, root cause analysis, project scoping, and evidence-based improvement.

children.title: Structured Problem Solving
children.description: Students learn repeatable ways to move from symptoms to root causes.

children.title: Problem statement, scope, objective, constraint, assumption, and deliverable
DMAIC, PDCA, A3 thinking, 8D, and engineering design process
Current condition, target condition, gap, root cause, countermeasure, and follow-up
Project charter, stakeholder, sponsor, timeline, and success metric
Root Cause and Cause Analysis Tools
children.description: This subtopic equips students with practical diagnostic tools.

children.title: Five whys, fishbone diagram, cause-and-effect matrix, and Pareto chart
Process observation, gemba walk, check sheet, and stratification
Failure mode and effects analysis, severity, occurrence, detection, and risk priority number
Hypothesis, evidence, validation, and avoiding blame-focused analysis
Improvement Project Execution
children.description: The point is to turn analysis into implemented change.

children.title: Baseline measurement, pilot test, implementation plan, control plan, and standard work
Before/after comparison, sustainment, audit, and handoff
Change management, stakeholder communication, and training
Benefit estimate, hard savings, soft savings, and lessons learned

topics.title: Data, Statistics, and Analytics for Industrial Engineering
topics.description: Show how IE uses data to understand variation, forecast performance, and support decisions.

children.title: Operational Data Basics
children.description: Students learn what kinds of data IE problems usually produce.

children.title: Cycle time, wait time, demand, defects, downtime, inventory, arrivals, and service times
Continuous data, discrete data, categorical data, time series, and event log
Data collection plan, sampling plan, operational definition, and measurement system
Missing data, outlier, duplicate record, timestamp, and unit consistency
Descriptive and Inferential Thinking
children.description: The goal is to understand variation before making decisions.

children.title: Mean, median, standard deviation, range, percentile, histogram, and boxplot
Common-cause variation, special-cause variation, sampling error, and confidence interval
Correlation, regression, hypothesis test, p-value, and practical significance
Capability, forecast error, and prediction interval as IE applications
Analytics and Visualization
children.description: Students see how analysis supports communication and action.

children.title: Dashboard, control chart, scatterplot, run chart, Pareto chart, and heat map
Excel, Python, R, SQL, BI tool, and data table
Data cleaning, transformation, aggregation, and reproducibility
Insight, recommendation, caveat, and decision support

topics.title: Operations Research and Optimization Overview
topics.description: Survey deterministic decision models used to allocate scarce resources and improve systems.

children.title: Optimization Modeling Language
children.description: Students learn the basic grammar of operations research models.

children.title: Decision variable, objective function, constraint, parameter, feasible region, and optimal solution
Linear programming, integer programming, binary variable, and mixed-integer model
Sensitivity analysis, shadow price, reduced cost, and binding constraint
Solver, spreadsheet model, algebraic model, and model validation
Classic Deterministic Models
children.description: This subtopic surveys the IE models students will meet later in depth.

children.title: Product mix, blending, workforce scheduling, assignment, transportation, and transshipment
Shortest path, minimum spanning tree, maximum flow, and network design
Facility location, set covering, lot sizing, and cutting stock as advanced examples
Model assumption, objective trade-off, and interpretation
Decision and Trade-Off Analysis
children.description: The point is to frame optimization as disciplined decision support, not magic.

children.title: Cost minimization, profit maximization, service maximization, and risk reduction
Single objective, multiobjective, weighted score, and Pareto frontier
Scenario, what-if analysis, robustness, and sensitivity
Ethical constraints, fairness constraints, and stakeholder criteria

topics.title: Stochastic Models, Queues, and Simulation Overview
topics.description: Introduce uncertain systems, waiting lines, random arrivals, and simulation as IE modeling tools.

children.title: Uncertainty in IE Systems
children.description: Students learn why randomness changes system behavior.

children.title: Random arrival, random service time, demand uncertainty, machine failure, and processing variability
Probability distribution, expected value, variance, and empirical distribution
Poisson arrivals, exponential service, normal variation, and triangular estimate
Risk, uncertainty, variability, and buffer
Queueing Concepts
children.description: This subtopic introduces waiting-line behavior common in service and production systems.

children.title: Arrival rate, service rate, utilization, queue length, waiting time, and system time
Single server, multiple server, finite capacity, and priority queue
M/M/1, M/M/c, bottleneck, and pooling effect as introductory ideas
Call center, clinic, checkout line, repair shop, and production queue examples
Simulation Concepts
children.description: The point is to model complex systems when formulas are too simple.

children.title: Discrete-event simulation, entity, event, resource, queue, and clock
Replication, warm-up period, random seed, confidence interval, and validation
Input modeling, output analysis, animation, and scenario comparison
Simulation software, spreadsheet simulation, and Monte Carlo preview

topics.title: Manufacturing and Service Systems Overview
topics.description: Compare production and service environments, process types, flow patterns, and operational trade-offs.

children.title: Manufacturing Systems
children.description: Students learn common production environments and their flow logic.

children.title: Job shop, batch production, assembly line, continuous flow, and cellular manufacturing
Routing, setup, work center, bill of materials, and production order
Throughput, WIP, cycle time, capacity, bottleneck, and line balance
Make-to-stock, make-to-order, engineer-to-order, and mass customization
Service Systems
children.description: This subtopic shows that IE also improves intangible, customer-facing work.

children.title: Service encounter, customer arrival, service blueprint, front stage, and back stage
Waiting time, service level, no-show, appointment scheduling, and triage
Healthcare, banking, hospitality, transportation, retail, and government services
Customer experience, reliability, responsiveness, and service recovery
Capacity and Flow Trade-Offs
children.description: The goal is to compare systems using flow, variability, and capacity concepts.

children.title: Little's Law, takt time, bottleneck rate, throughput time, and utilization
Batch size, setup time, transfer batch, and lot splitting
Capacity cushion, demand seasonality, and resource flexibility
Flow efficiency, responsiveness, and cost trade-offs

topics.title: Work Design, Methods Engineering, and Human Factors
topics.description: Introduce work measurement, ergonomic design, safety, and the interaction between humans and systems.

children.title: Methods Engineering and Work Measurement
children.description: Students learn how IE improves work methods with evidence and respect for workers.

children.title: Method study, work simplification, standard work, and best-known method
Time study, work sampling, predetermined time systems, and standard time
Allowance, rating factor, normal time, and observed time
Process chart, two-hand chart, and motion economy principles
Human Factors and Ergonomics
children.description: This subtopic centers the fit between people, tasks, tools, and environments.

children.title: Anthropometry, posture, reach envelope, visibility, and control-display compatibility
Cognitive workload, mental model, attention, fatigue, and human error
Manual materials handling, lifting equation, repetitive motion, and musculoskeletal disorder risk
NIOSH, OSHA, workstation design, and safety culture
Safety and Human-Centered Systems
children.description: The point is to treat people as system designers and system users, not interchangeable labor.

children.title: Hazard, risk, near miss, incident, and hierarchy of controls
Job safety analysis, standard operating procedure, and training design
Usability, accessibility, inclusion, and worker participation
Automation, human-machine interface, and decision support

topics.title: Quality Fundamentals, Statistical Process Control, and Six Sigma
topics.description: Explain quality as conformance, capability, variation reduction, and customer-focused improvement.

children.title: Quality Concepts
children.description: Students learn quality as both customer value and process capability.

children.title: Quality, grade, conformance, fitness for use, customer requirement, and critical-to-quality characteristic
Defect, defective unit, nonconformance, rework, scrap, and warranty
Cost of quality, prevention cost, appraisal cost, internal failure, and external failure
ISO 9001, quality management system, and continuous improvement
Statistical Process Control
children.description: This subtopic introduces variation monitoring and process stability.

children.title: Common cause, special cause, control limit, specification limit, and rational subgroup
X-bar chart, R chart, individuals chart, p chart, c chart, and u chart
Run rule, out-of-control signal, process stability, and false alarm
Process capability, Cp, Cpk, sigma level, and yield
Six Sigma and Quality Improvement
children.description: The goal is to connect statistical tools to structured improvement.

children.title: DMAIC, define, measure, analyze, improve, and control
DPMO, sigma level, defect opportunity, and rolled throughput yield
Voice of customer, CTQ tree, and measurement system analysis
Green Belt, Black Belt, control plan, and sustainment

topics.title: Lean Systems, Continuous Improvement, and Waste Reduction
topics.description: Introduce lean thinking, value streams, flow, pull, standard work, and continuous improvement.

children.title: Lean Principles
children.description: Students learn the language of value, flow, pull, and continuous improvement.

children.title: Value, value stream, flow, pull, perfection, and customer-defined value
Muda, mura, muri, and the eight wastes
Kaizen, gemba, respect for people, and standard work
Toyota Production System, jidoka, just-in-time, and takt time
Lean Tools
children.description: This subtopic gives students practical tools for observing and improving flow.

children.title: 5S, visual management, kanban, Andon, SMED, and poka-yoke
Value stream map, current state, future state, process family, and takt calculation
Cellular layout, one-piece flow, supermarket, and heijunka
A3 report, daily management, and leader standard work
Continuous Improvement Culture
children.description: The point is to see lean as a management system, not a toolkit checklist.

children.title: Psychological safety, suggestion system, coaching, and problem-solving routines
Standardization and improvement as paired activities
Sustainment, audit, metric review, and escalation process
Risks of superficial lean, tool copying, and cost-cutting misuse

topics.title: Supply Chains, Logistics, Inventory, and Facility Layout Overview
topics.description: Survey the flow of materials and information across facilities, inventories, transport, and networks.

children.title: Supply Chain Structure
children.description: Students learn how products and information move across organizations.

children.title: Supplier, manufacturer, distributor, retailer, customer, and reverse logistics
Material flow, information flow, cash flow, and demand signal
Procurement, sourcing, production, warehousing, transportation, and fulfillment
Bullwhip effect, lead time, service level, and coordination
Inventory and Logistics Basics
children.description: This subtopic introduces buffers and movement decisions.

children.title: Cycle stock, safety stock, pipeline inventory, reorder point, and economic order quantity
ABC analysis, stockout, fill rate, and inventory turnover
Mode choice, shipment consolidation, routing, and last-mile delivery
Warehouse, picking, packing, receiving, slotting, and cross-docking
Facility Layout and Location
children.description: The point is to connect physical arrangement to flow, cost, safety, and service.

children.title: Process layout, product layout, cellular layout, fixed-position layout, and hybrid layout
From-to chart, relationship chart, load-distance score, and block layout
Facility location, service area, center-of-gravity method, and network trade-offs
Material handling, aisle design, storage density, and worker travel

topics.title: Engineering Economics, Project Management, Ethics, and Sustainability
topics.description: Connect IE decisions to costs, schedules, stakeholders, ethics, sustainability, and professional responsibility.

children.title: Engineering Economics for IE Decisions
children.description: Students learn that improvement ideas must be economically defensible.

children.title: Fixed cost, variable cost, labor cost, overhead, savings, and avoided cost
Cash flow, present worth, net present value, payback period, and return on investment
Cost-benefit analysis, sensitivity analysis, and break-even point
Hard savings, soft savings, opportunity cost, and implementation cost
Project Management Basics
children.description: This subtopic helps students plan and execute small IE projects.

children.title: Scope, deliverable, milestone, task, dependency, and resource
Gantt chart, critical path, PERT, risk register, and issue log
Stakeholder analysis, communication plan, and change control
Project closeout, lessons learned, and benefits tracking
Ethics and Sustainable Systems
children.description: The point is to improve systems responsibly.

children.title: Professional responsibility, data ethics, worker privacy, and conflict of interest
Safety, equity, accessibility, and human dignity
Sustainability, energy use, waste, emissions, circular economy, and life-cycle thinking
Trade-offs among productivity, people, profit, planet, and resilience

topics.title: IE Tools, Software, Communication, and Capstone Mini-Project
topics.description: Introduce common IE software, modeling tools, visualization, communication, and project reporting.

children.title: Common IE Tools and Software
children.description: Students learn what tools support analysis, modeling, and communication.

children.title: Excel, Solver, Python, R, SQL, Tableau/Power BI, Minitab, and JMP
Arena, Simio, AnyLogic, FlexSim, and discrete-event simulation tools
AutoCAD, facility layout tools, ERP/MRP systems, and process mining tools
Version control, documentation, reproducibility, and file organization
Technical Communication
children.description: The goal is to turn analysis into a recommendation others can understand and act on.

children.title: Executive summary, problem statement, method, results, recommendation, and appendix
Chart selection, dashboard design, annotation, and data storytelling
Assumption, limitation, sensitivity result, and implementation risk
Presentation, poster, memo, and stakeholder briefing
Intro IE Mini-Project
children.description: The final project lets students practice the IE mindset on a real or simulated system.

children.title: System selection, stakeholder need, baseline data, and process map
Root cause analysis, metric definition, and improvement alternatives
Estimated impact, cost, risk, and implementation plan
Final report, oral presentation, and reflection on IE career interests
